Who this is for

Built for owners who carry the risk personally

Safer Together works best with businesses of roughly 10–50 people that hold valuable customer or payment data, rely on an outsourced IT provider, and have no dedicated security leader. If that sounds familiar, the question is rarely whether to improve — it’s where to start, and in what order.

THE SITUATION

You’re the security department

Decisions about access, vendors, and backups land on the owner’s desk — between everything else. You need judgment you can borrow, in plain language, on a schedule that respects the business.

THE GAP

Your IT provider keeps things running

That’s their job, and it matters. But keeping systems running and deciding how much risk the business should accept are different jobs. Safer Together does the second one — and checks the first.

THE RISK

Most attacks start with a person

Phishing, payment fraud, executive impersonation, and now convincing deepfakes bypass technology entirely. Safer systems need smarter teams — trained, rehearsed, and given simple rules to follow.

The framework

One shared map: NIST CSF 2.0

Every engagement is organized by the six functions of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 — the same language your customers, insurers, and vendors increasingly use to evaluate you. Pick a function to see what it means at small-business scale.

How engagements grow

Start small. Prove it. Stay ready.

Most clients begin with the fixed-scope Baseline Sprint — a low-friction first yes with a clear deliverable. From there, the work grows only if the value did.

RUNG 01 — START

Start

A fixed-scope Security Baseline Sprint with a clear deliverable: your gaps, ranked by business impact, and a 90-day roadmap.

  • Fixed scope, defined timeline
  • Owner debrief included
  • No obligation to continue
RUNG 02 — STRENGTHEN

Strengthen

Stay ready

Clear boundaries

What Safer Together is — and isn’t

What you get

  • Independent advice and training, from a senior practitioner
  • Priorities ranked by business impact, in plain English
  • Plans rehearsed before you need them — tabletop-tested
  • A second set of eyes on your IT provider’s security work
  • Progress you can see, in quarterly KPIs

What it isn’t

  • Not implementation — your team or IT provider installs and operates controls
  • Not emergency response — no 24/7 on-call or live incident response for hire; the work is preparation
  • Not a tool reseller — no commissions on products recommended
  • Not a replacement IT department — direction and review, not help-desk

Services · Advice & training only

Senior security judgment, right-sized.

The strategic thinking of a security leader, focused on the decisions and safeguards that matter most to your business — including the governance decisions the NIST CSF 2.0 Govern function puts in the boardroom.

Every engagement is scoped individually and quoted in a custom proposal. Safer Together advises and trains; your team or IT provider implements and operates. Incident work is preparation only — see the boundary note below.

How it works

From first call to a plan you own

1

Fit conversation

A short call about your business, your concerns, and your timing. If it isn’t a fit, you’ll hear that plainly — and get a pointer to who might be.

2

Scoped proposal

A fixed, written scope: what will be reviewed, what you’ll receive, and when. No open-ended billing, no surprise add-ons.

3

The work

Reviews, interviews, and working sessions with you and — where useful — your IT provider. Findings are explained as they emerge, not saved for a dramatic reveal.

4

Debrief & roadmap

You leave with ranked priorities, a 90-day roadmap, and the language to explain both to partners, customers, or a board.

The engagement ladder

  • Start — Security Baseline Sprint (fixed scope)
  • Strengthen — 90-Day Security Program, plus workshops as needed
  • Stay ready — Fractional Security Lead, ongoing

The boundary, stated plainly

  • Safer Together sells preparation, not rescue: incident plans and rehearsals, never 24/7 emergency response.
  • If you are in an active incident right now, call your IT provider, your cyber insurer, or law enforcement first.
  • Implementation stays with your team or provider — that keeps advice independent.

About · Karel Baloun, founder

Three decades building technology. One practice making it safer.

Karel has spent his career building, leading, and explaining technology businesses — from inside Facebook in its earliest days to the owner’s chair of his own companies. Safer Together is where that experience becomes practical help for small businesses.

Why a founder runs this practice

Most small businesses don’t fail at security because they don’t care. They fail because security advice arrives as jargon, fear, and a shopping list — with no one accountable for putting it in order. Karel’s background is unusual precisely because it covers both sides of that problem: deep platform engineering on one side, and a master’s in social psychology — how people actually behave, decide, and get fooled — on the other. Add formal cybersecurity training at UC Berkeley, with a capstone on disinformation defense, and you get the practice’s premise: safer systems and smarter teams are one problem, not two.

Safer Together LLC is Delaware-registered and was formed in 2020. It operated as a cybersecurity consultancy from May 2022 through December 2024; this site marks its relaunch, with a tighter, advice-and-training model.

Why rent judgment instead of hiring it? With information-security roles projected to grow 29% (BLS, 2024–2034), senior judgment is expensive to hire; Safer Together rents it by the project.

Off the clock, Karel is part of the ultrarunning community — most recently CTO of UltraSignup, the registration platform for trail and ultra races — and works in English, Japanese, and Czech.

The thread

A career in six chapters

2005 – 2006 · FACEBOOK

Built at internet scale

Facebook’s first senior software engineer — architected a product, led its team, and worked on the database stability and performance problems of a site growing faster than anyone expected.

2007 · AUTHOR

Explained the inside story

Wrote Inside Facebook, one of the first books about the company — an early exercise in translating how technology organizations really work for people outside them.

2007 – 2014 · I2WE / THRUSOCIAL

Built and led a company

CEO of i2we, creator of more than 300 Facebook apps and the thruSocial platform. The company was acquired by LEAP Commerce, where Karel continued as CTO — learning security from the owner’s chair, where cost and staff behavior are inseparable from the technical answer.

2018 – 2020 · UC BERKELEY

Cybersecurity, formally grounded

Master of Information and Cybersecurity at the UC Berkeley School of Information. Capstone: disinformation defense — how AI-driven inference can spot coordinated manipulation. Builds on an earlier M.S. in Social Psychology from UC Santa Cruz.

2020 – 2024 · SUNNYTIZE.ME

Acted when it mattered

Founded Sunnytize.me in the first weeks of the pandemic, producing 100,000 bottles of hand sanitizer and donating more than 30,000 — logistics, vendors, and trust under pressure.

2022 – TODAY · SAFER TOGETHER

The practice

Ran Safer Together as a cybersecurity consultancy (2022–2024), then served as CTO of UltraSignup (Dec 2024 – May 2025). Now relaunching Safer Together with a focused model: advice, training, and rehearsal for small businesses.

How the work is done

Three working principles

Calm over fear

Fear sells tools and freezes owners. You’ll get your risks straight — sized, ranked, and in plain words — so you can act on them in order.

People are part of the system

Every control eventually meets a busy human. Training, verification habits, and rehearsed decisions are security controls, not soft extras.

Independent, always

Advice-only means no products to sell and no implementation hours to protect. If the right answer is “your provider has this covered,” that’s the answer you’ll get.
